title: Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
snippet: Nothing like a little family togetherness in the morning. | Image: Apple Apple's ad introducing its new HomeView smart display is a little unusual. It's fast-paced and unruly, depicting a family of five as they rush through the morning routine. There's yelling and mess, misplaced keys and discarded eggshells. Apple's typical vibe is clean, simple, orderly; this commercial is chaos. But the spot has parents - those with teen children in particular - feeling seen. I'll admit that it stressed me out the first time I watched it, too. Mornings getting my five-year-old out the door are a special breed of chaos, and usually culminate in us playing whatever ad-libbed game will get him to put his shoes on. But it's not … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Apple’s ad introducing its new HomeView smart display is a little unusual. It’s fast-paced and unruly, depicting a family of five as they rush through the morning routine. There’s yelling and mess, misplaced keys and discarded eggshells. Apple’s typical vibe is clean, simple, orderly; this commercial is chaos.

But the spot has parents — those with teen children in particular — feeling seen.

I’ll admit that it stressed me out the first time I watched it, too. Mornings getting my five-year-old out the door are a special breed of chaos, and usually culminate in us playing whatever ad-libbed game will get him to put his shoes on. But it’s not quite as intense as this one, which features dad making French toast, mom losing and finding keys in her pocket, a proxy battle over the thermostat, a teenage boy helping himself to whipped cream from a can, and an unexpected video call. There’s also a microdrama about the daughter’s ride to school with a boyfriend nobody knew about that ends with everyone gathered around the HomeView watching the security camera feed of the two of them departing the porch. It’s a lot for just over three minutes of screentime.

If I know anything, though, I know to trust my colleague Jen Tuohy, senior reviewer and parent to two teens, on matters of the home. Her take? “The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone.”

Other parents of teens shared similar reactions on Threads. When tech analyst Benedict Evans posted about the ad feeling stressful and confusing, CNET editor at large Bridget Carey chimed in to defend it, saying “It was exactly what my morning is like and it was the most real ad I’ve ever seen from Apple.” Others agreed, saying it “accurately captured” real life and that it “hit home,” no pun intended, at least I think.

Even if Apple didn’t need to do much to heighten the stakes of a family getting out the door, there is of course plenty of sleight of hand at work when it comes to making the HomeView appear so essential. The family has seemingly drilled a hole directly into the middle of their kitchen island to accommodate the charging cable, for one. And what sibling is going to check a text message from a secret boyfriend on the communal kitchen screen with their brother sitting at arm’s length? I don’t believe any teenager trusts Apple’s privacy features that far.

The confusion about the commercial is understandable. This is a far cry from the quiet luxury lifestyle everyone seems to enjoy in Apple’s Vision Pro ads. There’s also Evans’ observation that the HomeView doesn’t really solve any of the problems that come up throughout the course of the video. In the case of a spontaneous FaceTime call from the grandparents, the screen in the middle of the kitchen seems to make things worse.

But maybe morning chaos isn’t the problem that’s being solved. If the alternative is five people all interacting with their own phones, then the HomeView presents a different picture where everyone gets the essential information they need from one shared screen and stays more present.

A screen that makes you be more present is a lovely idea, but the real test will come when it’s in real households. Is the HomeView going to be enough to convince families to put their personal devices down? Will everyone just ignore it and keep scrolling on their own iPhones? These are questions worth answering before you start drilling holes in your kitchen island! In any case, an ungovernable morning routine is probably a feature of a busy household, not a bug. Just ask a parent.

title: Google is ending support for Pixel Watch’s emergency LTE ‘Safety Signal’
snippet: Google launched the Pixel Watch 2 with “Safety Signal” to ensure users could use Emergency SOS and Safety Check without a Bluetooth or cellular signal. Now, those features require a phone or internet connection. more…
fullText:
Google launched the Pixel Watch 2 with “Safety Signal” to ensure users could use Emergency SOS and Safety Check without a Bluetooth or cellular signal. Now, those features require a phone or internet connection.

The Pixel ecosystem offers a few different life-saving features under the Safety app, which works both on the Pixel Watch and Pixel phones. That includes Emergency SOS for quick access to emergency services, and Fall Detection, which alerts others when the person wearing the watch takes a hard fall and might not be able to contact someone themselves. But it needs a connection to work.

	

All of those still worked for Fitbit Premium, and then for Google Health Premium users on the Pixel Watch 2 or 3 LTE models, as long as the watch didn’t have a Bluetooth or cellular plan connected. Safety Signal essentially allowed the Pixel Watch 2 or 3 to connect to LTE services for that emergency situation – a solid reassurance that those features would work without your phone or a carrier plan.

Google says support for Safety Signal will end on December 12, which means that the safety net won’t exist for much longer. Google says users who are subscribed to Google Health Premium will get an email notification letting them know 30 days prior to the final shutdown. Safety Signal will be operational until that transition period is over.

	

Safety Signal was just the fallback connection plan. Google’s existing standalone safety features will still work with another connection method:

Safety Check

Emergency Sharing

Emergency SOS

Fall Detection

Even though this feature only worked for the Pixel Watch 2 and 3, and then only for the LTE models, it’s still a huge loss.

title: Apple’s two HomeViews have one big hidden difference
snippet: Today Apple unveiled HomeView, its long-awaited smart home hub. The HomeView comes in two distinct models, one with a domed speaker base and the other designed for wall mounting. But there’s a hidden feature difference beyond the form factors. more…
fullText:
Today Apple unveiled HomeView, its long-awaited smart home hub. The HomeView comes in two distinct models, one with a domed speaker base and the other designed for wall mounting. But there’s a hidden feature difference beyond the form factors.

HomeView speaker system is much more powerful on model with domed base

If you’re trying to decide which HomeView form factor to buy, there’s a key detail you should know about.

Beyond the obvious design differences between the model with a domed base—‘HomeView’—and the one designed for your wall—‘HomeView (Wall Mounted)’—there’s a disparity in capabilities too.

The standard HomeView has a much more powerful speaker system built in. Here are Apple’s descriptions of each speaker setup:

HomeView delivers room-filling sound with support for Spatial Audio, making it a great way to enjoy music and podcasts at home. Its custom-engineered acoustic system combines a down-firing woofer and two full-range drivers to produce deep bass and crisp highs. Powered by the A18 chip and built-in sensors, computational audio continuously optimizes the loudness and bass response at any volume. 

HomeView (Wall Mounted) brings full, balanced sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement, along with support for Spatial Audio.

Echoing this, Apple’s technical specs page confirms both models have two custom full-range drivers, but the HomeView with domed base adds:

Custom down-firing woofer

Dual force-cancelling passive radiators

Essentially, if you want the best sound experience from your HomeView, you’ll want to buy the standard model.

But if audio quality isn’t as important to you, the wall-mounted version will probably get the job done. It still has built-in speakers, but it won’t deliver the same performance and thus isn’t as well-suited for everyday music playback.

title: M6 MacBook Pro: Three new upgrades launching later this month
snippet: Apple has a new M6 MacBook Pro launching later this month with a 14-inch screen and the current industrial design. And with its M6 chip, there are three upgrades we can expect from the new MacBook Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple has a new M6 MacBook Pro launching later this month with a 14-inch screen and the current industrial design. And with its M6 chip, there are three upgrades we can expect from the new MacBook Pro.

#1: Dual 16-core Neural Engine

If AI is in any way significant to your workflows—and with macOS 27’s AI features, it will be for more users—then the M6 MacBook Pro could be a big upgrade.

That’s because the M6 chip includes a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, up from the standard 16-core version available in M5 and prior. Per Apple:

M6 also introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, providing up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations to make on-device AI workflows run even faster. System frameworks can automatically utilize both engines simultaneously, enabling applications to see faster model execution.

#2: 12-core CPU and GPU with powerful new cores

The base M6 chip offers a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU. Both are solid upgrades over the M5, which was limited to 10 cores each.

M6’s CPU cores are especially interesting, as Apple is bringing three distinct core types to its base chip for the first time. It has 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. Here’s what Apple says about each core:

Super cores: “blaze through single-threaded workloads”

Performance cores: “use less power and join the super cores to run demanding multithreaded workloads”

Efficiency cores: “handle everyday background tasks”

Previously only M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra provided super cores and performance cores in a single chip. But now these Pro-level capabilities are available for standard M6 users.

#3: Major efficiency gains to likely improve battery life

M6 is the first Apple chip built on a new 2nm process. And the company says that brings the benefit of “a major leap in performance and power efficiency.”

Currently the only product with an M6 is the new Mac mini, which doesn’t run on a battery.

But in the MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and other upcoming M6 products, the new chip’s “major leap” in power efficiency is likely to enable longer battery life.

Apple could always opt to shrink the physical battery to offer comparable performance as before, but here’s hoping it uses M6’s improved efficiency to deliver better battery life instead.

snippet: The Fitbit Air is finally getting another band option that isn’t fabric or polyurethane. Instead, the Metal Mesh band might actually take the Fitbit Air up a notch. more…
fullText:
The Fitbit Air is finally getting another band option that isn’t fabric or polyurethane. Instead, the Metal Mesh band might actually take the Fitbit Air up a notch.

Band selection for the Fitbit Air has been limited. The Elevated Modern band and Performance Loop options are good, but they lack a little flair. The Fitbit Air needed another band option to take advantage of just how easy it is to swap styles.

The Metal Mesh band fills that gap. It comes in Polished Silver and Champagne Gold with the intent of matching your existing jewelry. The look lets the wearable blend in with an elevated outfit, even if the Performance Loop band does a good job fitting most looks.

Google says the Metal Mesh band for the Fitbit Air will be priced at $69.99. You’ll also be able to buy the Fitbit Air with the Metal Mesh band and the Performance Loop band for $149.99 as a bundle, but it only comes in gold. That’s $20 more than the special editions, like the Steph Curry band and the Pokémon Sleep band, but it comes with two bands instead of a single option.

	

Packed into the band announcement, Google detailed a couple more feature additions to the Fitbit Air, regardless of band choice.

Google announced Health Guardian features that analyze your overall health picture. For Google Health Premium users who set up blood pressure and insulin resistance trends in the app, a report will be available each month to guide lifestyle adjustments. This may give the AI Health Coach some more usability for the average Fitbit user.

Google also notes that automatic activity tracking is getting an overhaul. According to the new post, Google claims the improvements will result in “more intelligent, accurate, and reliable” tracking.

Tracks more activities: We expanded the number of activities your Fitbit tracker or Pixel Watch can detect from 10 to more than 100, including strength training, swimming, and racket and team sports.

Uses more context: Powered by contextual reasoning, Google Health factors in critical context — including your workout routines, historical data, manual edits, and, with permission, your location — to deliver nearly 2x more accurate detections and cut missed workouts by more than half. 7

Logs workouts automatically: Workouts that meet your minimum duration threshold (15 minutes by default) with a sustained elevated heart rate are automatically logged, and a summary is sent to your mobile app, typically within 30 minutes.

Learns your patterns: When you confirm or edit an activity, you’re improving a feature that learns your unique patterns and uses them to refine its predictions.

These updates are planned for “later this month.” This comes as the company recently announced a more expensive $179 tracker called the Fitbit Edge. Unlike the Fitbit Air, this model has a screen carrying Google’s Material You design language.

As for the new Metal Mesh bands, Google has them available for pre-order on its website and at Target. It looks like the new bands should ship later this month.

title: Fairphone’s latest repairable earbuds are smaller, lighter, and longer-lasting
snippet: The Fairbuds 2 have had a total design revamp from the original pair. Repairable, ethical phone brand Fairphone has released its second pair of earbuds. The Fairbuds 2 are just as repairable as the first generation, but deliver improved audio and almost twice the battery life. The Fairbuds 2 are out now in the UK and Europe from £99 / €119, and a US launch at $119 will follow on November 2nd. The Fairbuds 2 have been redesigned from the ground up, moving to a stemmed design, available in black or green, and a case that's 37 percent smaller than the first generation. Despite that shrinking hardware, Fairphone has almost doubled the buds' battery life, which now totals 40 hours without active noise cancellation … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Repairable, ethical phone brand Fairphone has released its second pair of earbuds. The Fairbuds 2 are just as repairable as the first generation, but deliver improved audio and almost twice the battery life. The Fairbuds 2 are out now in the UK and Europe from £99 / €119, and a US launch at $119 will follow on November 2nd.

The Fairbuds 2 have been redesigned from the ground up, moving to a stemmed design, available in black or green, and a case that’s 37 percent smaller than the first generation. Despite that shrinking hardware, Fairphone has almost doubled the buds’ battery life, which now totals 40 hours without active noise cancellation, with eight hours on the buds alone, dropping to six with ANC on. Charging is over USB-C, and takes a couple hours for a full top-up. Sadly Qi wireless charging isn’t supported — though it isn’t on Apple’s $129 AirPods 5 either.

I never used the original Fairbuds, but sound should be improved here thanks to new bio-cellulose dynamic drivers, though still at the same 11mm size, plus refined ANC and new support for the LDAC codec. Multipoint connectivity supports two devices at once, and a five-band EQ in the app lets you fine-tune audio.

The new charging case is 37 percent smaller and 32 percent lighter.

Charging is only via USB-C though.

The buds and case come in either green or black.

That silicone sleeve is removable, and is how you open the earbuds up for repairs.

I’ve been using the Fairbuds 2 for a couple of weeks, and while I wouldn’t say they’re the most polished or premium earbuds you’ll find for $120, I’ve got no real complaints either. They look great, the simple touch controls work well, and audio quality is good, if a little muddy at times, lacking the expansive sound stage of some other buds. The ANC has impressed me too, cancelling out most background noise I’ve wanted rid of.

Of course, the main reason to buy Fairbuds is the repairability, which remains relatively unique — though European legal changes will force other manufacturers to catch up soon. Here, Fairphone has concentrated on matching what it offered in the first Fairbuds, but that’s still impressive: the battery in each earbud can be removed in less than a minute without any tools, while a single T5 screw is all that’s between you and the cell in the case. Spare parts will be sold on Fairphone’s site, with a total of seven user-replaceable parts, including the eartips and sleeves. An IP54 rating guarantees some additional measure of protection against rain and sweat, though not complete waterproofing, and a three-year warranty should deliver a little extra peace of mind.

You won’t need anywhere near this many screw bits to repair the Fairbuds 2.

There’s a single Torx T5 on the bottom of the case, and no screws at all on the buds.

It only took a minute or two to disassemble the buds and case, even without instructions.

Crucially, all three batteries are removable and replaceable.

The other side of Fairphone’s promise is transparency about its production and materials. The company says that 49 percent of the materials in the Fairbuds 2 are “fair and recycled,” including recycled plastics and rare earth minerals, and cobalt, gold, and silver sourced with fair mining credits. It also says the buds themselves are assembled under fair working conditions.

title: Indie App Spotlight: ‘Milepost’ is a driving journal that saves your memories on the road
snippet: Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. fullText:
Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. If you’re a developer and would like your app featured, get in contact.

Milepost turns your roadtrips into more of a journey. It lets you record all of your drives, and journal all of the key moments that happened along the route, so your roadtrips become a lot more memorable – rather than just a blip of time.

Top features

Most people drive a ton, but a lot of the experience is forgotten once you reach the destination. Milepost helps you keep track of that, by letting you save the route, distance, speed, time, and weather. You can also take notes, add photos, and make it into a true gallery, which the app calls roadbooks. The roadbook serves as a true timeline of your journey, and you can even tie in Apple Music to see what you were listening to while driving.

Milepost isn’t just about your own drives though, it’s also meant to be a social experience. You can share your journeys with friends with its built in social network, and they can also comment and react to what you share. The app also has a well-designed garage experience where you can share what cars you have.

	

The app supports Siri, Shortcuts, as well as CarPlay. It’s available on all Apple platforms, including the Mac, where you have a larger view to get a more detailed look at your drive. Beyond that, it also offers an MCP server so you can plan future trips with your agents based on what you’ve done in the past.

Download the app

Milepost is available for free on the App Store for the core experience, but if you subscribe to Milepost Pro, you unlock full drive history, the ability to share more designs, alternative app icons, as well as driving insights. Milepost Pro is $4.99/month, $29.99/year, or $199 lifetime. It’s available with a 7 day free trial.

The new Apple TV 4K is available to pre-order now and ships November 13. But its $299 price tag may put off prospective upgraders.

If you just want the new Siri Remote, you can order that instead.

From Apple’s press release:

The new Siri Remote is compatible with Apple TV HD and Apple TV 4K, and is also available for purchase separately.

The latest Siri Remote has the same basic design as the prior model. But it adds Precision Finding support for Find My, and a built-in speaker so you can play a sound on the remote when it’s lost.

title: If a Chromebook wasn’t for you, Googlebook isn’t either
snippet: Let’s not pretend; if you weren’t sold on a Chromebook, Googlebook isn’t for you either. more…
fullText:
Let’s not pretend; if you weren’t sold on a Chromebook, Googlebook isn’t for you either.

In our review of Googlebook as a platform, Abner Li explains how this platform sets a foundation for a potentially fascinating future. But, even from that viewpoint, it’s hard to ignore the shortcomings. Between the app gap and plenty of overlooked mistakes throughout the OS, Googlebook is far from a “finished” product.

In many ways, it continues to resemble what it’s replacing, ChromeOS, and that’s not going to leave the best impression for everyone.

Chromebook launched to a market starved of capable and reliable cheap laptops, and at a time where even higher-end machines were inherently compromised. Better battery life, no virus protection, simpler setup, price, take your pick, a Chromebook was a genuinely good choice for quite a while. But, as time went on, that math started to shift away from Google’s favor. I’d argue that it’s harder to find a bad laptop than it is a good one now, and there are good options on every price point, whether you’re looking at Windows or a MacBook. There’s an abundance of fully-capable Windows machines with long battery life and plenty of power, and frankly, the MacBook Air is $1,099.

	

With that in mind, Googlebook’s inherent similarities to ChromeOS betray any progress it might have made.

Under the hood, the new Android base is a much better foundation for the years to come. On the surface, where the users are, Googlebook hasn’t addressed any of the issues ChromeOS was dealing with, at least from a functional level. Apps are the biggest problem, as everything from mainstays to the niche library of apps are a shell on Googlebook of what they are on Windows and macOS. Unless you’re heavily using the web or Android apps for everything you do, you’re going to run into times where Googlebook is simply incapable of doing the things you want. And that even goes for Google’s own product offerings. Within the past week Google announced a new app that could combine voice recordings, shorthand notes, and local AI processing to build out detailed notes of a meeting or presentation. It’s a really useful and fun idea, but you literally cannot use it on Googlebook — it’s exclusive to Mac. 

Even the whole “this is a laptop for Android users” schtick doesn’t hold any water. These features are nonexistent at launch for most users, and ChromeOS had the vast majority of these anyway. 

	

Put simply, Googlebook isn’t a reset from ChromeOS. It’s not catching up to the competition. It’s the same old problems (plus a few new ones) in an admittedly much faster and more polished new chassis. The future might tell a different story but, at least for now, Googlebook is not for you if a Chromebook wasn’t.

snippet: SpaceX has announced plans to make Starlink Mobile a “major mobile carrier in the US” thanks to two major new developments. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
SpaceX has announced plans to make Starlink Mobile a “major mobile carrier in the US” thanks to two major new developments. Here are the details.

SpaceX announces two milestones toward making Starlink Mobile a full-fledged mobile carrier

Starlink Mobile might soon be a full-fledged mobile carrier option for your iPhone. 

SpaceX announced this week two big developments to accomplish this goal.

A new “nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio”

FCC approval for Starlink Mobile’s Gen2 constellation application

	

The former is a major milestone in the journey toward Starlink Mobile becoming a genuine alternative to other mobile carriers. From the announcement:

While Starlink Mobile’s global 2 GHz mid-band spectrum will provide high-bandwidth capacity in the United States, this new low-band spectrum will provide a coverage layer that ensures Starlink Mobile’s signal penetrates through obstacles, such as walls, and can provide service to customers’ devices even when they are in buildings. Critically, most existing mobile devices already support this underused band.

Final FCC approval hasn’t been granted yet, but SpaceX anticipates it will be and the company can move forward with deploying “a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment.”

The FCC has approved, however, the deployment of 15,000 satellites that are optimized for 2 GHz spectrum globally. These V2 Starlink Mobile satellites deliver “more than 100 times” the bandwidth of the current generation, boosting connection speeds globally.

title: IDC: Mac shipments drop 11% in Q3 as global PC market slides 20%
snippet: Despite seeing an 11% drop in Mac shipments during Q3 2026, Apple’s market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5%, as the broader market saw shipments plunge 20.1%, according to a new report from IDC. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Despite seeing an 11% drop in Mac shipments during Q3 2026, Apple’s market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5%, as the broader market saw shipments plunge 20.1%, according to a new report from IDC. Here are the details.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market under challenging conditions

IDC today released a report on worldwide PC shipments for Q3 2026, noting that Apple significantly outperformed the broader market despite shipping fewer Macs than a year ago.

According to IDC’s preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs during Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the year-ago period.

The overall PC market, however, fell much more sharply, with worldwide shipments dropping 20.1% year over year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple’s share of worldwide PC shipments actually increased from 8.5% to 9.5%.

This kept Apple in fourth place, behind Lenovo, which topped the ranking with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% share, followed by HP with 10.3 million shipments and a 16.5% share, and Dell with 7.6 million shipments and a 12.1% share.

HP recorded the steepest year-over-year decline among the top five vendors, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS, meanwhile, saw the smallest decline, down 8.6% year over year, with 5.5 million shipments and an 8.7% share.

	

Here’s IDC:

Vendors and channels bought inventory earlier in the year ahead of price hikes, pulling demand out of Q3. Combined with continued supply constraints, that left the quarter without its usual seasonal lift and pushed shipments below both Q2 and last year.

Looking ahead, IDC says that “channel concern over high inventory and soft demand at elevated prices could bring promotions in the near term,” adding that “pricing will stay well above year-ago levels.”

The firm also says that the economy has weakened since the previous quarter, which could further reduce demand and “darken the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027.”

title: Googlebook Glowbar doesn’t have the ‘knock-knock’ Chromebook Pixel battery gesture
snippet: One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before. more…
fullText:
One of the beloved features of Google’s original big push into laptops, the Chromebook Pixel, is getting a revival in Googlebook’s Glowbar, but it very much feels like a hollow version of what came before.

The original Chromebook Pixel launched in 2013 as the launchpad for ChromeOS. To this day, it remains a pretty incredible piece of hardware design, though it was inherently flawed with a truly atrocious display and a sky-high price tag to boot, not to mention an even more restricted operating system compared to what ChromeOS would eventually morph into. Still, it earned a follow-up in 2015’s Chromebook Pixel which delivered a lot of key upgrades.

Both models included a signature hardware feature in the four-piece “light bar” across the top of the lid. It was mainly a design element to ring in the Chrome connection with the four colors of the Chrome and Google logos. It lived on in the later, yet short-lived Pixel C tablet. 

It also served a somewhat practical purpose, too.

	

When you would plug in a Chromebook Pixel, the light bar would give you a rough idea of how much charge was already in the battery. Beyond that, a fun little “knock-knock” gesture on the lid would tell you the same information, but whenever the laptop was just out. You could tap the lid and get an idea of the battery status without opening it up or plugging it in, which was especially useful in a time where laptop battery was still very much Not Great.

It’s that gesture that’s gone on Googlebook’s Glowbar, which retains the light-up action when you plug it in, but loses the “knock-knock” that really grabbed everyone’s attention when Google first launched it. 

What can the Glowbar do? 

Like Chromebook Pixel, it does light up when you plug the machine into power, showing battery status both when it plugged in and unplugged. Useful! It’s also more granular than it was on that older hardware. The only other function, besides an animation when you close the lid, is interaction with Gemini. I struggle to see the utility in that one given the Glowbar is at the back of the display, but I guess why not?

title: iOS 27.0.1 is now Apple’s recommended update for users still on iOS 26
snippet: Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed. more…
fullText:
Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed.

iPhones running iOS 26 will default to iOS 27.0.1 as next update

Over the last few years, Apple has started rolling out its major new iOS updates more gradually.

For example, while iOS 27 officially became available to all users on September 14, it wasn’t featured as the default, top-level update in the Settings app.

Instead, until very recently, users saw iOS 26.7 as the recommended update, while iOS 27 was minimized under a small ‘Also Available’ section in the Software Update screen.

Apple does this because inevitably, despite a months-long beta process, there are often new bugs that emerge following the public launch. And the company wants the chance to address these before pushing the update to its full user base.

But now with iOS 27.0.1 available, Apple has made iOS 27 the default update for users still on iOS 26.

	

So the next time those users go to Settings ⇾ General ⇾ Software Update, they’ll see iOS 27.0.1 featured prominently.

Users will still have the option of staying on iOS 26. But we can expect to see iOS 27 adoption accelerate now that Apple has made it the primary update in Settings.

Last year Apple waited until after iOS 26.1 was available before recommending the switch from iOS 18. So pushing iOS 27 much earlier this year is a clear endorsement of the company’s focus on bug fixes and stability with its latest major update.

fullText:
Last year, Kuxiu was the first to make chargers that perfectly match the Cosmic Orange iPhone. They released their 3-in-1 X40 turbo and their S4 Solid State battery pack. They both matched the orange color so well that it seemed as if they were 1st-party accessories. This year, the new hero color for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup is burgundy, and Kuxiu is back at it again with a new matching burgundy D5 5-in-1 charging station. With its premium build quality, perfect color matching, built-in cooling, and price, this charger is everything you need from a performance and aesthetic standpoint.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video below!

Kuxiu D5 specs & features

I reviewed their original D5 a few months back, and it was one of my favorite chargers of the year. Now they have brought it all back with some awesome-looking accents and features. The Kuxiu D5 is advertised as a 5-in-1 charger because it charges three devices but also features a built-in cooling fan and a diagnostics display. You get:

Qi2.2 25W wireless charging

Retractable Apple Watch charging puck

AirPods charging mat

Built-in cooling fan that can be manually turned off and on

Smart color display to give us real-time charging stats

Includes 45W charging brick and braided cable in the packaging

While it is not as compact as something like their X40 Turbo, there is still some thought put into portability and travel with this charger. The Qi2.2 charger can fold down flat into a small cube you can take wherever you need, and the Apple Watch charger retracts into the charger as well. For me, it has worked best as a permanent desk charger, but it’s nice to know that it is also portable. 

My experience

As I mentioned, I have been using the original black color for a few months as my main desk charger. It is reliable, functional, and simple to use. So when Kuxiu announced their Burgundy version, I knew I had to check it out, especially since I was looking for some Burgundy color-matching accessories for my new iPhone 18 Pro. 

Since I knew this charger was already great, I wanted to see how closely the color matched the iPhone 18 Pro, and I was impressed by how identical it was. The aluminum parts of the D5 match the Burgundy on the iPhone 18 Pro, and they add other burgundy accents across the charger’s different materials. 

Beyond the aesthetics, my favorite part is the built-in cooling fan because it adds tangible value to the setup. I am someone who constantly installs new iOS betas, tests new features, and puts my phone through situations where it tends to get warm. So, having the active cooling system built directly into the charger has been game-changing in keeping my phone efficiently cooled and helping it sustain 25W charging for longer, since it does not get warm. The fan is also dead silent, but if you do want to turn it off, you can do so with one tap. Then, of course, you have the diagnostics display that shows you all the charging stats you need to see from all the active chargers. 

Pricing & availability

The Kuxiu D5 is available today on Kuxiu’s site in the original Space Grey and their new Burgundy color. You also get the required 45W charging brick and a braided USB-C cable. It is currently on sale for $59.99. 

Final take

For under $60, I challenge someone to find me a high-quality 3-in-1 charger that offers all the features above and includes all the charging accessories you need to use it at its best. That is why Kuxiu is one of the brands I recommend the most; it’s the performance-to-price ratio that sets them apart. So if you just picked up a new Burgundy iPhone or you are in the market for a new 3-in-1 charger, I highly recommend checking this one out. My only wish is that the next version has a USB-C port so you can charge a 4th device, like a smart ring or something. Otherwise, this thing is great.

macOS 27: What’s new for iPhone Mirroring 

The biggest change for iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now adjust the size of the iPhone Mirroring window with any iOS 27-compatible apps. Right now, that means it only works for Apple’s native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, support for resizing will expand rapidly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only support three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. The change in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27 clearly indicates Apple is prepping for the foldable iPhone Ultra, expected to launch later this year.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27 also has several other updates:

Control Center access

DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring did not support accessing Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it with the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut or with the “View” menu in your Mac’s menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos using iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would simply show a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was enabled.

macOS 27 also has a new app icon for iPhone Mirroring, just like it does for many other stock Apple apps.

title: Apple planning huge iPhone Duo demo experiences at select retail stores: report
snippet: iPhone Duo is just about two weeks away from releasing, and according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has big retail plans ahead for its first foldable iPhone, to make sure every customer gets to see it to the fullest. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo is just about two weeks away from releasing, and according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has big retail plans ahead for its first foldable iPhone, to make sure every customer gets to see it to the fullest.

Apple is gearing up for a major launch with the iPhone Duo, which should be no surprise. What is a surprise though, is the amount of attention Apple is putting into making sure this launch goes as smoothly as possible.

In the newsletter, Gurman reports that the company is planning to have over a hundred demo units at some of its biggest stores:

The company is preparing a major retail push, with a huge number of demo units at its flagship stores. The Fifth Avenue location in New York City is expected to have more than 150 units across hands-on demo stations and in-store fixtures. The Apple Park Visitor Center at the company’s home base, meanwhile, will have nearly 100. Other locations, including Michigan Avenue in Chicago, the Grove in Los Angeles and the Upper West Side in Manhattan, will each have roughly 30 to 40 units.

Some of its smaller stores will only have around 20 units, which still seems bigger than usual, given the fact that there are only two colors. Given how hard it’ll be to buy a Duo at launch, allowing a lot of hands-on demos at once seems sensible.

iPhone Duo demo fixtures

Beyond the number of demo units, the company has also designed a new MagSafe stand that can hold an unfolded iPhone Duo, alongside two “standard” iPhones (likely iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.) There’ll also be iPhone Duo demo units without a security tether “along the sides of stores,” so users can demo StandBy mode and other features.

Lastly, the company is planning a new fixture for some Apple Stores that showcase the iPhone Duo opening and closing, so it’s “impossible to miss” when you walk into an Apple Store.

All in all, iPhone Duo will become the forefront of Apple Stores after its launch on October 23rd. It’ll be hard to get, so if you’re interested in owning one – make sure you’re geared up to preorder it on October 16th.

title: Apple Home adds two powerful new features in iOS 27
snippet: Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27.

#1: HomeKit Secure Video packs big upgrades in iOS 27

HomeKit Secure Video is Apple’s secure, cloud-based service included with iCloud+ for compatible video cameras. It lets you record footage, view it from anywhere, and set up activity automations.

In iOS 27, Apple Intelligence powers three new HomeKit Secure Video upgrades (via Apple):

Generated video descriptions: “users can quickly understand what happened across a sequence of video clips, even without watching them.”

Search in clips: “[users] can easily find what they’re looking for, like a package delivery.”

Noteworthy clips: “At the top of the Search page, the Home app elevates noteworthy clips that users may want to review, so they can quickly see important moments.”

Joining these is a fourth feature, not powered by AI, that’s been on users’ wishlists for a while: 4K video. Apple says, “supported HomeKit Secure Video cameras can now stream and record in 4K.” Previously, 1080p was the max resolution.

If you’re looking for a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, I’d recommend:

Aqara G100 2K security camera: Excellent budget-friendly option currently only $33

eufy 4K security camera: For 4K support if you have more to spend

#2: Real-time notification updates

Most of the Home app’s upgrades this year focus on HomeKit Secure Video. But there’s also another AI-powered new feature: real-time updating notifications.

Here’s how Apple describes it:

The Home app draws on Apple Intelligence to understand related notifications as a single activity, so users receive one notification that updates as the activity happens.

Inside a new Apple Intelligence section of the Home app’s settings screen, you’ll see a ‘Reduce Notifications’ toggle. It explains: “Combine related activities, such as someone arriving and unlocking the door, in one notification that updates in real time.”

Essentially, Home app notifications will stop showing outdated information, and only focus on the latest, most relevant info.

So instead of seeing the seven related notifications above, you’ll get one alert that says: ”Lydia arrived. Checked the mail. Garage Door was closed.”

title: Apple challenges Taction’s $5.7B patent verdict, says damages were based on ‘guesswork’
snippet: Apple is asking a federal judge to overturn a $5.7 billion verdict in a patent infringement lawsuit brought by Taction Technology over the Taptic Engine used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple is asking a federal judge to overturn a $5.7 billion verdict in a patent infringement lawsuit brought by Taction Technology over the Taptic Engine used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Here are the details.

’Impermissible guesswork on a massive scale’

A few weeks ago, a jury ordered Apple to pay $5.7 billion for infringing two patents held by Taction Technology, which are related to the Taptic Engine that currently powers haptic feedback across its devices.

At the time, Apple said it strongly disagreed with the jury’s verdict and the damages awarded, which it called “entirely unsupported by the facts.”

Apple stressed its technology was “fundamentally different” from what is covered by Taction’s two patents, and announced plans to appeal.

Today, Apple filed a new motion asking the court to overturn the jury’s verdict, arguing that Taction failed to present sufficient evidence to support any damages award, let alone $5.7 billion, which the company notes is “the largest patent verdict in history, by more than $3 billion.”

Apple adds that before the trial, the court excluded the analysis by Taction’s damages expert due to flaws in how the expert calculated royalties from a previous licensing agreement, and that the expert was later barred from testifying altogether.

Apple also notes that Taction never presented evidence establishing how much its patented technology was worth. Instead, it simply asked jurors to award whatever they considered a reasonable royalty, leaving them “with no choice but to engage in impermissible guesswork on a massive scale.”

From Apple’s motion:

Taction told the jury it was “just looking for a reasonable royalty for its contribution,” […], but never offered evidence of what that contribution was worth. Instead, it asked the jury to “award a reasonable royalty that y’all think is appropriate.” […] Taction failed to meet its burden to present evidence that would allow the jury to “adequately tie a dollar amount to the infringing acts,” […]. Without any such evidence, the jury was left to speculate, contrary to the Court’s instructions and binding Federal Circuit case law.

Apple also notes that, before the award was announced, the judge told attorneys he was “not sure that the figure that appears on the verdict form is what the jury meant to convey,” raising questions about whether the $5.7 billion figure was what the jury actually intended.

In a more striking accusation, Apple argues that one of Taction’s key technical experts, Dr. Oliver, relied on a “rigged” test to support his findings of patent infringement.

In essence, both Taction patents in question describe a technology designed to produce consistent vibrations across different frequencies. Apple argues that its Taptic Engine works differently, producing much stronger vibrations at certain frequencies than at others.

The company goes on to allege that Dr. Oliver developed a new testing method specifically for the lawsuit, which measured how Apple’s electronic control system could regulate the Taptic Engine’s vibrations, rather than whether the underlying hardware met the patents’ requirements.

From the filing:

No reasonable juror could find that “the output of the transducer is highly damped” in the accused products, as required by the Court’s construction. Rather than assess highly damped output by using the test in the patent, Taction’s infringement theory rested on a legally erroneous test rigged by Dr. Oliver for this case. The only evidence of the transducer’s actual output, including Taction’s pre-filing and infringement contentions testing, was introduced by Apple and those tests showed a peaked response that Dr. Oliver conceded was not highly damped.

Finally, Apple argues that if Taction’s interpretation of its patents is accepted, the patent claims at issue would themselves be invalid. According to the company, the testing method used to establish infringement contradicts the method described in the patents, making it impossible to clearly determine what the patents actually cover.

For these reasons, Apple is asking the court to overturn the jury’s verdict, rule that Taction is entitled to no damages, and find that Apple did not infringe the (possibly invalid) patents. Alternatively, the company is requesting a new trial covering infringement, patent validity, and damages.

With Apple’s motion now filed, and the jury’s verdict not yet formally entered as a final judgment, the court will now consider whether to uphold the $5.7 billion award, overturn the verdict, or order a new trial.

What’s your take on Apple’s arguments? Let us know in the comments.

title: Mike Tomlin’s Minecraft World Is the Talk of the Internet, but How Good Is It Really?
snippet: The former Steelers coach built the sprawling city brick by brick with a video game console controller.
fullText:
Football coaches have the freedom to create their own worlds on the playing field. But retired Steelers legend Mike Tomlin took a different route — manifesting his vision block by block within a massive Minecraft city. What started as a shared family project with his children evolved into a solitary, 12-year labor of love. Now, the sheer depth of Tomlin’s digital city is capturing widespread attention online.

Tomlin served as the Steelers’ head coach for 19 seasons before resigning in January, having never finished with a losing record. 

His video was released Oct. 1 and received more than 3 million views in less than two weeks. In the video, Tomlin shows off an expansive Minecraft city, complete with sports stadiums, high-rise apartments, homes and other buildings. He began working on the city about 12 years ago after watching his kids and their friends play Minecraft when they were in middle school, building it in the game’s creative mode with their help.

			

More from CNET

“I was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time,” Tomlin says in the video. “I’m certainly not skilled enough in video game play or have the stick control to [play the game’s survival mode], so I got interested in this creative mode. I like to build, I’ve always had an interest in architecture, and so I started doing this creative city as a means to spend time with them.”

His kids eventually outgrew the game and moved on to different ones, high school and eventually college. That left Tomlin to work on the city by himself, which he did off and on for years while still coaching the Steelers.

“More than anything, it was therapeutic for me, some mindless entertainment,” Tomlin says. “I’m not a big TV watcher. It allowed me to detach from the realities and pressures of life.”

Tomlin spends the rest of the video showing viewers around the place, focusing on his basic, early-days architecture, penthouses, apartments and how he tried to design a solid urban space. He plans to release more videos to discuss different buildings, the city’s design and other elements of his sprawling city. 

How wonderfully weird

The sprawling city features high-rises, sports stadiums and water features.Mike Tomlin

Leading up to the video’s release, there was no indication whatsoever that Mike Tomlin played computer games. That helped make his big Minecraft debut all the more delightful. The 54-year-old coach showed off thousands of hours of playtime in a 19-minute video, and no one could believe it. 

“12 years of Minecraft? Didn’t you know this? Did nobody know this?” asked a shocked Ty Schmidt, producer and on-air personality of the Pat McAfee show,  on an episode of the show. 

The sports world finally saw what some Minecraft fans already knew: Tomlin’s dedication to the game is unmatched.

“We’re talking block by block,” McAfee said. “He had 14 30-story buildings around a body of water that he wanted to build his city around — one block at a time! They all got patios! He had a penthouse with a shark aquarium. It was unbelievable.”

Minecraft fans, too, showed up to explore the coach’s dazzling feat. Many were surprised to learn that he built this on the Bedrock edition of the game using a video game console, beginning with PlayStation 3 before moving on to PlayStation 4 and 5. That means Tomlin didn’t have access to the mods that many builders use in the Java version of the game on PC, or the freedom that a mouse and keyboard provide. He built his city one brick at a time on a PlayStation controller. 

Tomlin was initially unaware of his viral fame. In an interview on Late Night with Seth Meyers, Tomlin said he was at a gala with his phone off when the video went live, and it wasn’t until later that his kids told him about the massive response. Tomlin had caught up by the time he appeared on Football Night in America with NBC on Sunday night. 

“I’m appreciating all of this, to be quite honest with you,” Tomlin said during the broadcast. 

How good are Tomlin’s designs?

Tomlin dedicated his entire 20-minute video to discussing architecture.Mike Tomlin

The spectacle of Tomlin’s Minecraft city is one of those wholesome events that had viewers smiling all weekend, except a few Steelers fans who were probably already pretty mad about losing to the Cleveland Browns less than 24 hours after the video was released. That didn’t stop a lot of people from wondering whether Tomlin’s city is actually as good as it looks. It turns out that most of the Internet agrees that it lives up to the hype.

“From my understanding, [it’s a] phenomenal Minecraft city,” McAfee said. “Like, as I was watching it, I was like, man, the attention to detail [is outstanding].”

Noted Minecraft city builder Alpine1 was one of the first to create his own video on the topic, and he was impressed. He had some suggestions for Tomlin, recommending that the coach consider using glass panes instead of glass blocks and more sophisticated floor designs, such as installing tile floors in showers. But Alpine1 did note that Tomlin likely started building the city before many modern building tools were available to Minecraft players. 

“This is really awesome to see,” Alpine1 said in the video. “I’ve been advocating for people to build Minecraft cities for years because there’s so much you can do… and I think Mike has really captured this.”

Zach Nagel, an architecture student from the University of Cincinnati’s School of Architecture and Interior Design, also took a stab at analyzing Tomlin’s city in a separate video. He noted that Tomlin used some concepts that are actually practiced in architecture, specifically adding a penthouse with an aquarium right across the street from a full-sized aquarium. 

“Now, what Coach Tomlin is talking about here, having a central theme to the building, is a term that we use in architecture as well, the parti,” Nagel says. “If you talk to 20 architects and ask them to give a definition of a parti, you might get 20 pretty different answers. At its [simplest], a parti is a single idea or scheme that drives all of the decisions you make in a building.”

Nagel goes on to praise Tomlin for not only considering the building’s exterior appearance but also its interior design and the functional needs of the city’s fictional residents. He says that a lot of Tomlin’s design choices and approach are in line with what some architects use. 

“In another world, he could’ve totally gone down this career path had he wanted to,” Nagel says. “And I’m glad to see that Minecraft remains such an accessible tool for those who want to shape the environment around them.”
excerpt:
Football coaches have the freedom to create their own worlds on the playing field. But retired Steelers legend Mike Tomlin took a different route — manifesting his vision block by block within a massive Minecraft city. What started as a shared family project with his children evolved into a solitary, 12-year labor of love. Now, the sheer depth of Tomlin’s digital city is capturing widespread attention online.

Tomlin served as the Steelers’ head coach for 19 seasons before resigning in January, having never finished with a losing record.

fullText:
OxygenOS, the flavor of Android for OnePlus devices, is officially going away as the brand steps out of the global market, with Oppo’s ColorOS taking over starting with Android 17. And, now, we have an official list of OnePlus devices getting Android 17 starting later this month.

title: Where Google Wallet state IDs are available on Android
snippet: States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android. more…
fullText:
States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android.

Update 10/10

How to add your state ID on Android

Open the Google Wallet app on Android 9+

Tap the “plus” button next to “View more” at the bottom

Choose “ID & personal info” and then “Driver’s license or state ID” 

Select your state and follow the instructions

The process involves taking a picture of the front and back of your physical card, as well as a short video of yourself for verification: a “photo from this video will be submitted to your ID issuer.” 

Once approved, the ID will appear below the carousel of payment methods alongside other passes. The order can be rearranged, while you can remotely remove the ID online if your phone is missing: myaccount.google.com > Personal Info > Manage IDs.

	

Related: Google Wallet rolling out stacked card list redesign on Android

What Google Wallet state IDs are supported

Arizona (Rolled out October 2023)

Arkansas (Rolled out October 2025)

California (Rolled out August 2024)

Colorado (Rolled out October 2023)

Georgia (Rolled out October 2023)

Iowa (Rolled out June 2025)

Maryland (Rolled out December 2022)

Montana (Rolled out August 2025)

New Mexico (Rolled out December 2024)

North Dakota (Rolled out October 2025)

Ohio (Rolled out September 2026)

[New] Oklahoma (Rolled out October 2026)

Puerto Rico (Rolled out October 2025)

Where state IDs are coming next

Google previously said to expect support in the following places:

West Virginia (Upcoming availability announced April 2025)

Where you can use state IDs

The primary place you can use this digital ID is at TSA checkpoints in some US airports. There are two ways to do so, starting with tapping your phone at the NFC terminal. You then review the information that will be shared with the TSA and authenticate with device unlock. There’s also a QR code method that requires opening the ID in Google Wallet. 

Officially, you still have to carry the physical ID card at all times.

Some apps, like from car rental services, are beginning to accept digital IDs for identity and age verification. On mobile, if an app or website requests your age, it’s as simple as confirming (and authenticating) that you want to share this information with a system-level prompt/sheet. On desktop web, the experience involves scanning a QR code. 

Google wants to make it possible to do that “without any possibility to link back to a user’s personal identity” through what it calls Zero-Knowledge Proof. This technology will be open-sourced for anyone to use. 

Looking ahead, the IDs can be used at DMVs in Arizona, Georgia, Maryland, and New Mexico as part of “improved and streamlined customer experiences.”

	

Google is also working on letting you use digital IDs to “recover Amazon accounts, access online health services with CVS and MyChart by Epic, verify profiles on platforms like Uber and more.”

Using passport as REAL ID

Google in April pointed out how you can “use your ID pass created from a U.S. passport with TSA security for domestic travel at supported airports, even if you do not have a REAL ID driver’s license or state-issued ID.” This comes ahead of the May 7, 2025 deadline. 

To do so, open Google Wallet > Add to Wallet > ID pass. This three-step process involves taking a picture of your passport’s info page, and then scanning the security chip found inside the back cover of your passport. You also have to record a video of your face that Google will review “to make sure you’re a real person, and compare the video to your passport photo to make sure you’re the owner of the passport.”

The NFC and QR code instructions for using this digital passport ID are unchanged from above. You also have to keep the physical version on you when traveling. As a reminder, this won’t work internationally.

title: Amazon’s new Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad lineup some much needed competition
snippet: This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets. They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well. more…
fullText:
This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets. They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well.

First and foremost, I want to make it quite clear that I’m not saying the iPad is doomed or anything remotely close to that. However, I do think the Alexa Tablet serves as a real form of iPad competition, which the iPad has generally lacked.

New Alexa tablets serve as strong competition

Amazon is putting a lot of care into these tablets that other Android manufacturers haven’t, and while these tablets come in at lower price points – they certainly punch above their weight class.

There are three Alexa Tablets to start off the lineup: an 8.7” model at $229, an 11” model at $329, and a 12” Pro model at $499. To me, the one in the middle is the most interesting.

It offers 8GB of RAM, a 90Hz display, a thin design, and a similarly sharp display. That compares to the budget iPad, which comes in $120 higher with less RAM, a lesser display, and a thicker design. Granted, the iPad has the A16 chip, which probably feels much faster than the MediaTek chip powering it. The iPad also starts at 128GB, compared to the 64GB on the Alexa Tablet. Once you upgrade the Alexa Tablet to 128GB, there’s only a $70 difference.

Hardware wise, the Alexa Tablets seem pretty competent. Obviously, Android on tablets isn’t going to be quite perfect, but given its tie in with Alexa and the fact that the tablet is priced quite well, I could see a lot of people wanting to buy these, even if they potentially would’ve considered iPads. Of course, one strong suit from Amazon is the Kindle experience, and these Alexa Tablets offer a reader mode that cuts blue light.

Wrap up

Only time will tell, but Amazon might make a pretty big dent into the tablet market with its new entries. Even the 12” Pro at $499 seems like a really worthwhile product. At the very least, I hope some strong competition means Apple will be less complacent with its iPad upgrades. For example, the iPad Air has largely only received chip upgrades since its last redesign in 2020.

	

I’m personally excited to try one of these out and truly put it to the test. Right now, Amazon also offers 20% off with any trade-in, making it an even better deal.

What do you think of these new Alexa Tablets? Would you consider getting one of these for a friend or family member during the holiday season? Sound off in the comments.

title: Gemini ‘Task’ redesign integrates Spark into the main chat app
snippet: In addition to revamping settings and the navigation drawer, Google is combining its Spark personal agent with the main Gemini chat experience. more…
fullText:
In addition to revamping settings and the navigation drawer, Google is combining its Spark personal agent with the main Gemini chat experience.

This redesign adds buttons for “Chat” and “Task” just above the prompt box. “Task” is Gemini Spark, with Google explaining that there’s now a “new home for Spark: Start new tasks anytime and keep track of them in your chats.”

Old vs. new

As part of this change, “Spark” disappears from the navigation drawer, while a new “Scheduled” page is introduced. This surfaces Spark tasks and Scheduled actions, with the feed organized by Active, Paused, Completed, and Suggested. 

	

Meanwhile, the list of conversations at the bottom is no longer called Recents. All chats and Spark tasks are combined into one history. The new filter icon lets you sort by All, Ready, Needs attention, and In progress.

Google appears to be deemphasizing the “Spark” branding with this redesign. Another example is how “Gemini Spark Settings” in the account menu has been renamed to just “Task settings.” 

This change is rolling out via a server-side update on Android. We’re not seeing it just yet on iOS or the web. Gemini Spark requires an AI Pro or AI Ultra subscription.

Announced at I/O 2026 in May, Gemini’s 24/7 personal agent is now better integrated into the overall app with this update. It’s much quicker to start a task with the experience no longer siloed off.

title: Beats Reveals How to Buy Pokemon Portable Pill Speaker: Gotta Hear ‘Em All
snippet: Pikachu, we see you.
fullText:
Put a Pokemon character, especially Pikachu, on just about anything — including a $100 Polaroid camera — and fans will take notice. On Tuesday, Beats by Dre revealed the look of its upcoming Pokemon-themed Beats Pill Bluetooth speaker, as well as the cost and where to buy it.

Beats by Dre teased the collab on Monday, but confirmed it on Tuesday. The company’s social-media post and official website revealed that the special-edition Pokemon Beats Pill speaker will be available Thursday. While we guessed on Monday there might be two different Pills speakers, it turns out there’s only one, with two Pokemon characters on it. The speaker is shown with both a Pikachu image and one of Mimikyu, a sad Pokemon who disguises itself as Pikachu. 

The special-edition Pokemon Beats Pill will sell for $149.99 at Target and apple.com, and is already shown on Target’s website. It comes with the speaker itself, a removable lanyard and charm, and Beats x Pokemon stickers.

			

More from CNET

On Monday, Beats shared a teaser with the caption, “Time to catch something new,” which plays off the classic Pokemon tagline, “Gotta catch ’em all!” The 6-second video shows electrical charges in yellow and purple flashing over a shadowed Beats Pill speaker. It ends with a screen showing the Pokemon Poke Ball logo and the Beats by Dre “b” logo, with an X between them, teasing the product collaboration.

Apple bought Beats by Dre for $3 billion back in 2014.

The speaker isn’t a brand-new revelation for those who stay up-to-date on all things Pokemon. Last week, a Pokemon fan who goes by BritBrattv posted a photo to Facebook showing a bright yellow Pikachu-themed Beats Pill speaker in what appears to be a Target shopping cart, though that photo was not confirmed as official.

And former Apple CEO Tim Cook shared a video on X in August showing Pikachu visiting Apple Park.

“Today’s agenda at Apple Park,” Cook wrote. “Introduce the @Pokemon team to John, talk gaming and politely ask Pikachu to stay out of the pond. Two out of three were accomplished.” By “John,” he presumably meant John Ternus, the new Apple CEO.

Representatives for Beats by Dre and Pokemon didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

The Beats Pill speaker in non-Pokemon designs is priced at $129 at Target and Amazon as of Tuesday. In a 2024 review, CNET audio expert David Carnoy called the Pill “a very good compact Bluetooth speaker,” praising its sound quality and strong battery life.

title: PC Gamers, Rejoice: GTA 6 PC Port Could See Release in Early 2027, Report Says
snippet: The console release is still slated for next month, and a PC port might be coming sooner than anyone previously thought.
fullText:
PC gamers might not have to wait much longer to play Grand Theft Auto 6 after all, according to a new report from GamesBeat. A new leak, attributed to four industry sources familiar with developer Rockstar Games’ plans, points toward a PC port for the highly anticipated game happening within the first three months of 2027.

Despite multiple high-profile delays, Grand Theft Auto 6 for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S is still on for a Nov. 19 release.

If the latest reporting is true, the leak is another headache for Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive. The hype cycle for GTA 6 has been plagued by controversy, including the revelations that there will be no physical discs and that core features like certain car modifications and clothing shops will be locked behind the $100 “Ultimate edition” of the game.

			

More from CNET

A deluge of leaks from as far back as 2022 has made GTA 6’s development cycle shockingly transparent. The latest spoilers have been shared by a hacker group known as CyberLeek, which has continued to post new footage (and shill scammy cryptocurrency), despite the best efforts of Take-Two’s legal team.

In spite of the challenges Rockstar has faced in the lead-up to GTA 6’s release, analysts report blockbuster demand for the new game, with projections ranging from $3 billion to $5 billion in revenue during launch week.

A representative for Rockstar Games did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Rockstar’s PC ports usually come out at least one year after the console release date, so an early 2027 release would be a departure from the norm.Rockstar Games

Rockstar’s PC ports have always been slow. Why change now?

Rockstar has historically ported its games to PC well after their initial console release. PC gamers waited nearly two years for an official Grand Theft Auto 5 port, and a little more than a year for a Red Dead Redemption 2 port.

Rockstar’s delayed PC ports are often attributed to a host of optimization and debugging challenges, especially because PC gamers run games on more diverse hardware. Some critics argue that the company “double-dips” on sales by creating FOMO and driving PC players to consoles first. When a port is released, the thinking goes, the PC player will buy a second company and bolster Rockstar’s sales.

Either way, there are several reasons why Rockstar might be trying to turn around this particular port more quickly than ever before.

If the development studio is planning to quickly release an online service for GTA 6, that would be a massive revenue driver – the current iteration of GTA Online rakes in more than $1 million each day, and has surpassed $5 billion in revenue over its lifespan.

If a new version of GTA Online is planned for GTA 6, having the wider base of PC players will likely be more profitable in the long term than any “double-dipping” sales practice.

Also, while consoles have always been the most profitable platform for Rockstar’s games, the market is shifting. The RAMageddon chip shortage is pushing hardware prices higher, and home consoles are becoming more expensive – and less accessible.

While these hurdles also affect folks looking to buy an off-the-shelf computer or build their own PC, the market share of PC gamers is growing nonetheless. Newzoo analysts predict that there will be more than 1 billion PC gamers by 2028.

Most PC game spending is focused on microtransactions – so if one were to release a massive live service game with the ability to purchase, say, virtual preloaded debit cards, there’s probably no better time to do so.

title: Latest GTA 6 Leak of Nude Character Is a Bad Crypto Scheme Fundraiser
snippet: The leaker group is threatening to post the game’s full storyline ahead of its Nov. 19 release.
fullText:
As it nears a month before its long-awaited release, Grand Theft Auto 6 is again the subject of a high-profile leak, this time involving nudity of another main character. 

The online group Cyberleek reportedly posted new footage of one of the game’s main characters, Lucia, engaging in activities such as walking in public and skydiving nude. 

While there are indications that what was leaked is not from the final game — it could be an earlier developer build modded to allow for nudity — the leakers are threatening to post the game’s entire main storyline ahead of the Nov. 19 game launch. This follows a separate leak that featured the game’s other main character, Jason, also nude for much of a 24-minute video.

			

More from CNET

Reports say the leaked files have been made available on sites with a $40 paywall, but clips have appeared on free websites and social media. Cyberleek said it has other footage to release with names like “Police shootout,” “Beach massacre” and “Fight Jet” ahead of a full gameplay release.

The leakers are demanding that publisher Take-Two Interactive publicly apologize for not offering physical discs and issue a physical, disc-based version of the game. However, meeting these demands is highly unlikely. The game is set to be a digital-only release, and altering the production timeline at this stage is practically impossible.

There seems to be something else behind it, though: more money. Cyberleek is urging people to pump its self-named meme coin, threatening to leak a full build of GTA 6 if the coin reaches a market valuation of $30 million. As of this writing, it has ranged recently from about $2 million to $7 million, with news of the leak adding to its volatility.

A representative for Rockstar Games, the studio owned by Take-Two Interactive that built GTA 6, did not immediately return a request for comment. But the company has been involved in investigations into previous leaks and has expressed dismay about groups trying to spoil the game. 

In August, in response to leaks from the same group that included nine short gameplay videos, Rockstar posted on X that the leaks were “heartbreaking” and told players, “this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time.”

In late August, Rockstar finally gave fans a lengthy look at the game with 27 minutes of uninterrupted gameplay footage, which it made available on Netflix and YouTube. There was no nudity in that footage, but fans have been speculating how R-rated the final version of the game could get in terms of its sexual content.

Rockstar, which spent more than a dozen years developing the game, has been carefully orchestrating its rollout and working with authorities to shut down repositories featuring leaked assets.

The game will be released on PlayStation 5 consoles for $80 to $100, depending on the edition gamers purchase. It’ll also be available on Xbox Series X and S, and a PC Port is coming in early 2027.

He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

title: Google Cloud announces ‘Gemini agent’ as ‘universal agent for work’
snippet: At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers. more…
fullText:
At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers.

Gemini agent is a “new single, universal agent for work” available in the Gemini Enterprise app, Workspace, and third-party services. Google says you can “give it objectives, not instructions.” It can answer questions, handle knowledge work, create media, and write/run code.

“For example, if your manager emails you asking for the latest project update as a slide deck, Workspace Intelligence recognizes that as a delegatable task and gives you a single-click option to pass it to Gemini.”

…you can ask Gemini to set up a meeting with the usual team of regional event leads next week, without supplying a single name or email address. Gemini determines who those people are from the membership of your chat space and the thread from your last event, checks their calendars, and starts an email thread to coordinate a time that works, even with external participants.

Besides functioning as a personal assistant, the Gemini agent can serve as a “team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department.”

	

Under-the-hood, the Gemini agent “runs each job on the model that fits best.” This includes both the Gemini and Claude families of models today with support for other private and open models in the future. This is meant to “deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.” It uses sub-agents to “tackle multi-step tasks” and connects with various third-party tools. 

	

Gemini can communicate with these sub-agents to coordinate workflows, including parallel and sequential steps that can run for hours or days.

The agent runs in the cloud for a “single set of memories, context, and one personalization graph.” There are four kinds of memory: 

Session memory: “for the task in front of it, even when it runs for days”

Semantic memory: “a structured knowledge base it builds as it reads documents, talks to people, and works with other agents”

Procedural memory: “for how a job gets done, including skills it writes for itself:

Episodic memory: “everything it has done before”

In Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Chat, you can mention @Gemini to invoke. The Gemini agent is available from any device and channel, with command line, Google Workspace, Slack, and Microsoft 365 given as examples. An API allows it to be integrated into third-party applications to surface and operate as a “headless agent, meaning it does not need a dedicated user interface.”

The Gemini agent will see wide availability soon for Workspace customers with select Business and Enterprise plans. It’s currently in private preview.
