title: The iPhone Duo’s cooling system hides a clever trick inside its hinge
snippet: While a folding iPhone posed a new challenge for Apple’s thermal engineering team, they came up with a creative way to leverage the device’s hinge to their advantage. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
While a folding iPhone posed a new challenge for Apple’s thermal engineering team, they came up with a creative way to leverage the device’s hinge to their advantage. Here are the details.

iPhone Duo’s hinge features a flexible graphite pipe

PCMag recently sat down with Dan Murray, Apple’s vice president of silicon engineering, and Banafsheh Barabadi, the company’s senior manager of thermal product design, to discuss the architecture of the A20 Pro chip.

The new SoC, which powers the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo, is Apple’s first iPhone chip built on a 2 nm process, following the technology’s debut with the M6 chip in the Mac mini in August.

And while the A20 Pro was designed with all three new iPhones in mind, the iPhone Duo version packs some additional capabilities. These include a second display engine to run both screens simultaneously.

From PCMag:

The iPhone Duo’s A20 Pro variant is just slightly different. “For iPhone Duo, we added a second display engine to support simultaneous operation of the inner and outer displays,” says Murray, “and with the increased CPU and GPU performance, we ensure we can deliver a smooth user experience across the displays. For the inner display, we also added support for placing the FaceTime camera behind the display.”

The report offers a really interesting, in-depth look at the A20 Pro’s thermals and the new vapor chamber Apple developed to keep them at bay. That includes what Apple calls “metal over foam,” a material that iFixit also examined during its recent teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro.

The second pillar is a new material that bridges the gap between the A20 Pro and the vapor chamber. “We call it metal over foam,” says Barabadi, and it “basically creates a direct thermal and mechanically compliant coupling between the SoC and the vapor chamber. It is highly effective in removing the heat, meeting the strict mechanical requirements of the system. It took us months of development to get the material properties exactly right to be able to use this material.”

Perhaps the most interesting tidbit from the story is what Apple did to improve the iPhone Duo’s thermal performance, particularly given the challenges of dissipating heat in a device that doubles in thickness when folded.

From the report:

“This was one of the most technically challenging aspects of our design,” says Barabadi. To surmount the issue, Apple routed a flexible graphite pipe through the hinge itself to transfer heat between the two halves, thereby increasing the surface area available for heat dissipation. “This part need[ed] to be co-engineered between our thermal team and the mechanical team. It’s a flexible material that needs to survive, as you can imagine, many hinge cycles while maintaining its thermal connectivity, and also its structural integrity throughout the product life cycle.”

PCMag’s interview with Murray and Barabadi also goes into the A20 Pro’s architecture, including the benefits of placing the DRAM next to the processor rather than stacking it on top, and you can read it in full here.

title: Google announces $179 Fitbit Edge tracker with display, GPS
snippet: Google is following the Fitbit Air launched in May with a second tracker that features a screen called the Fitbit Edge. more…
fullText:
Google is following the Fitbit Air launched in May with a second tracker that features a screen called the Fitbit Edge.

The Fitbit Edge features a wide, pill-shaped AMOLED screen — protected by Gorilla Glass 3 — that offers 46% more display than the Charge 6 from 2023. The 11.5mm-thick body is made from precision-crafted aluminum with nano-molding technology to allow for a 40% more precise GPS (versus Charge 6), while there’s a dedicated altimeter for elevation tracking. On the right side, you’ll find a large button for tactile control, like when swimming. This device has IP68 / 5ATM dust and water protection.

On the underside, you’ll find the sensors. The Fitbit Edge has an accelerometer, altimeter, ambient light sensor, far-field skin temperature sensor, gyroscope, heart rate sensor, multipurpose electrical sensors (ECG), and red and infrared sensors (SpO2).

The Fitbit Edge uses the same magnetic USB-C charger as the Fitbit Air. A 5-minute charge gives you a day of battery, while a full top-up takes 90 minutes. Battery life is rated at a week with the always-on display disabled. When enabled, the Fitbit Edge comes in at around 2 days. Like the Pixel Watch 5, you can open the device to replace the battery.

	

The Fitbit Edge is available in the following colors:

Matte Black Aluminum case / Obsidian Active Band

Polished Silver Aluminum case / Fog Active Band

Satin Pyrite Aluminum case / Olive Active Band

Champagne Gold case / Canyon Active Band

The bands are replaceable with a new swap mechanism and four additional designs: 

$39.99 Active Sport: Made of “ultra soft silicone” with large pill-shaped cutouts

$59.99 Magnet Band: Clasp-free design with magnets embedded into the strap

$149.99 Metal Links

$49.99 Performance Loop: Stretch and micro-adjustable

Supporting Android and iOS, the Edge is running a Fitbit operating system similar to the Air. A larger screen unlocks a richer interface that takes inspiration from the Pixel Watch 5.

Google showed a dozen or so watch faces for the Fitbit Edge with analog and digital options. You can customize what complications appear via the Google Health app.

Swiping left/right from the watch face lets you access various tiles, with the order customizable. This includes Quick start (for different exercises), Focus metrics, Sleep, Heart, Cycle health, Weather, Timers, Alarms, and Music controls.

Compared to the Charge 6, music controls work with any app on your paired device, while phone notifications are also available. Quick replies to messages are limited to Android due to iOS platform limitations. You also get Google Maps navigation, but there is no Google Wallet given the lack of NFC.

	

The Exercise app lets you track over 50 types of activity with real-time guidance and workout views. The Fitbit Edge can connect to equipment with heart rate broadcasting. 

The Fitbit Edge (and the Air) feature upgraded automatic activity detection. This AI-powered contextual reasoning can learn your habits over time to add support for over 100 activities. 

You can have the Fitbit Air, Edge, and Pixel Watch 5 operate on the same account with seamless switching.

The Fitbit Edge costs $179.99 with pre-orders open today and availability on October 27. A Stephen Curry Special Edition is available for $219.99 with a custom band.

title: iPhone Air 2 is coming, here’s everything we know so far
snippet: Apple is working on a second-generation iPhone Air, and it could address several key limitations of the current model. Here’s everything we know about the iPhone Air 2, including features, release date, and more. more…
fullText:
Apple is working on a second-generation iPhone Air, and it could address several key limitations of the current model. Here’s everything we know about the iPhone Air 2, including features, release date, and more.

Will there be an iPhone Air 2?

The iPhone Air has reportedly sold worse than Apple expected. The Information reported in November that Apple had indefinitely delayed the release of a second-generation model due to those lower-than-expected sales.

Apple reportedly “notified engineers and suppliers that they were taking the next iPhone Air off the schedule without providing a new release date.”

Shortly thereafter, however, The Information updated its reporting to say Apple wasn’t canceling the iPhone Air 2 altogether and that one is still very much in the works.

iPhone Air 2 features

A second camera

One of the biggest tradeoffs of the ultra-thin iPhone Air design is that it only has one camera. This is reportedly something Apple is pushing to change for the iPhone Air 2.

According to sources including Bloomberg and The Information, the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera on the back.

Bloomberg says it will be an ultra-wide camera, not a telephoto camera. This would align it with Apple’s base model iPhones, which also have a main camera and an ultra-wide camera.

A20 Pro chip

The iPhone Air 2 will reportedly be powered by the A20 Pro processor, up from the A19 Pro in the current model.

The A20 Pro chip will be Apple’s first 2-nanometer iPhone processor. This new fabrication process will mean the A20 Pro can offer more power and be more efficient in a similar-sized footprint.

The chip will also use another new innovation called Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module, which integrates the SoC and DRAM at the wafer level for better performance and lower power consumption.

Better battery life

Apple is also reportedly working to improve the battery life of the iPhone Air 2.

According to a supply chain leak, the iPhone Air 2 will have a 3,500mAh battery. For comparison’s sake, the first-generation iPhone Air has a 3,149mAh battery, so this is an increase of more than 10%.

Beyond increasing the physical size of the battery, the iPhone Air 2 will likely offer longer battery life thanks to the efficiency improvements of the A20 Pro chip.

It’s important to remember, however, that there are many variables at play when it comes to an iPhone’s battery life. We’ll have to wait and see the exact numbers when Apple officially unveils the iPhone Air 2.

Vapor chamber

According to The Information, the iPhone Air 2 will feature a vapor chamber cooling system. Apple first debuted its vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, touting significantly improved heat dissipation and performance.

If Apple brings the vapor chamber to the iPhone Air 2, it means the device will stay cooler during high workloads and sustain high performance for longer periods.

iPhone Air 2: Release date

The iPhone Air 2 was originally expected to be released in September 2026 alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup.

Most recently, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple plans to release the iPhone Air 2 in spring 2027 alongside the new base model iPhone 18.

What do you think of Apple’s plans for an iPhone Air 2? Is Apple making the right changes and improvements? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Apple Mail added four convenient new features in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it packs key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it packs key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

Upgraded search

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a big upgrade.

From Apple’s website:

More relevant search in Mail. A new ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

I can’t count the number of times search has previously failed to find messages that I knew existed. So far in my testing, iOS 27 seems to have fixed that.

New suggestions that include third-party apps

Suggestions at the top of messages have been in Apple Mail for years. But in iOS 27, they get a new, more flexible design and expand to support third-party apps.

When Mail detects that you might want to take action on the contents of an email, a suggestion might appear at the top of the message. These include: directions in Maps, creating events in Calendar, tracking a shipment with Apple Wallet, and more.

In iOS 27, third-party apps can offer suggestions too. And when multiple apps are available with suggested actions, there’s a drop-down menu to show you all available options.

Smart Reply improvements

Smart Reply is a keyboard feature that automatically surfaces reply options you can utilize with a single tap.

In iOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence comes with improvements to Smart Reply.

Apple says that Smart Reply “can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.” Essentially, rather than offering fairly generic reply options, now Smart Reply suggestions will actually sound a lot more like you.

Siri AI capabilities

Apple has added ‘Ask Siri’ buttons throughout Apple Mail, just like the rest of its system apps. And Siri AI brings a bunch of new powers for Mail users.

One example I’ve seen several times on social media already is that you can ask Siri to delete all messages from a specific sender that’s spamming you.

Bug fixes

Beyond new features, Apple also says that iOS 27 makes the Mail app run better than ever thanks to bug fixes and performance improvements. Here are some specific examples given:

Faster message loading in Mail

More reliable search indexing in Mail

Improved list formatting in Mail

Improved unread badge accuracy in Mail

title: Apple’s frenetic HomeView video showed the one use-case for this device
snippet: The launch video Apple created to show off the long-awaited HomeView product couldn’t have been more different from its usual fare. While just watching it gave me a feeling of anxiety, I suspect it perfectly encapsulates the one use-case for this device … more…
fullText:
The launch video Apple created to show off the long-awaited HomeView product couldn’t have been more different from its usual fare. 

While just watching it gave me a feeling of anxiety, I suspect it perfectly encapsulates the one use-case for this device …

HomeView is cute. I said a couple of years ago that I hoped that Apple would lean into the quirkiness of the iconic iMac G4 design, and in my view the company has borrowed enough of that heritage while still making it look like a modern device. What was rather less cute was that launch video – but that’s not accidental.

I’m a minimalist who places a premium on a home which feels calm and organized, and the typical Apple product video bears a strong resemblance to what my home would look like if I had about ten times the income (space in London is expensive!). The HomeView video, in contrast, felt to me utterly chaotic.

I found it both frenetic and jarring. But I think that’s exactly the point. I’ve spent enough time in the homes of friends with teenage kids to get the sense that this is probably a pretty accurate picture of a typical weekday morning. It also depicts the one scenario I could see making sense for this device.

If you’re either single or live as a couple, then it’s hard to see too much benefit to a HomeView. It doesn’t do anything we can’t do on our own devices or on HomePods with the existing multi-user Personal Requests feature we’ve had since 2019. (And no, I don’t find the digital photo frame justification convincing simply because the display is so small.)

	

Of course, the same argument could be made about families with kids, but when you’re trying to gather everybody together around the breakfast table, then I can definitely see the appeal of having a single device in one place be the way everyone gets their digital needs met. It’s a more wholesome picture than each family member silently staring at their own iPhone.

How realistic a goal this is is something I will leave to the parents to advise, but it certainly strikes me as a valiant attempt.

If you’re a parent with teenage kids, did the video accurately depict a typical morning, and do you think a HomeView could bring everyone together in the way Apple hopes? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

snippet: Google Health 5.10 is rolling out as a smaller update this week with a trio of new features across the app. more…
fullText:
Google Health 5.10 is rolling out as a smaller update this week with a trio of new features across the app.

Version 5.10 is available on iOS and still rolling out for Android users:

Irregular Rhythm Notification in Japan: Irregular Rhythm Notifications are now available in Japan on Pixel Watch and Fitbit devices, analyzing your heart rhythm data in the background while you’re still or sleeping to check for signs of atrial fibrillation (AFib). Users in Japan can set up the feature in the Health tab in the Google Health app. Learn more about how it works and check supported devices in our Help Center.

Readiness Score Updates: Your Readiness Score now uses additional signals from your sleep for a more personalized experience.

	

Delete your logs by chatting: Logged something with your Google Health Coach by mistake? title: MagSafe Monday: This aluminum MagSafe wallet ejects your credit card with one click
snippet: My biggest annoyance with all types of wallets is when it This aluminum MagSafe card wallet takes a different approach with a side-mounted eject button that fans your cards up with a single press, so you can grab the one you need one-handed without pulling them all out. more…
fullText:
My biggest annoyance with all types of wallets is when it This aluminum MagSafe card wallet takes a different approach with a side-mounted eject button that fans your cards up with a single press, so you can grab the one you need one-handed without pulling them all out. 

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

The eject button is the best part

Hands down, the best part of this wallet is the eject button. The side button slides to fan your cards upward so you can grab whichever one you need without removing the wallet from your iPhone. This is the reason to buy this wallet over others as its the main unique thing. If you’re the type who keeps one card in a wallet and never needs to choose between them, a basic slot MagSafe wallet is probably fine. If you’re carrying two or three cards and want to pick the right one quickly at checkout, the ejector earns its keep.

The wallet is machined from lightweight aluminum with a scratch-resistant finish, and it comes in a bunch of different colors if you want it to match your iPhone or case. The wallet uses 32 built-in magnetic strips to snap onto a MagSafe compatible iPhone. I haven’t used it long enough to know how the finish holds up, but it feels solid.

The aluminum housing claims it blocks 13.56MHz RFID frequencies, so your contactless credit cards and ID are protected from electronic skimming in airports, etc. This is worth knowing upfront: this wallet holds up to 3 cards. That covers most everyday carry setups, but if you’re someone who needs four or five cards accessible, this isn’t the right fit. Three cards, one eject button, and a metal build is the whole point here. If this held 5 cards, it would honestly be perfect.

I wish it had Find My support, but it doesnt. If Find My matter to you, you’ll need to look elsewhere, but if you want a clean metal MagSafe wallet with a fast card ejector and solid MagSafe hold, this does this job well.

Wrap up

The eject button is what makes this MagSafe wallet worth buying. This one has a mechanism that actually speeds up the process of getting a card. The RDID blocking functionality is also pretty nice as well. The Metal housing is not something I’ve used in a wallet before, so it’s been a change, but overall I like it. Again, the downside is that it’s limited to 3 cards only.

You can buy it from Amazon.

Apple has officially set its Valentine’s Day offering for 2027: a new romantic comedy series named Prodigies.

Prodigies will premiere February 10 with its first two episodes, followed by weekly releases every Wednesday through March 17.

The series stars Will Sharpe (“The White Lotus”) and Ayo Edebiri (“The Bear”), and was created, written, directed, and executive produced by Sharpe.

From London to Tokyo by way of Virginia, this unconventional take on a romantic comedy explores ideas of potential, ambition and the universal complexities of long-term relationships. As they begin to question whether their very ordinary existence is living up to the extraordinary promise of their childhood, they find themselves in a new and terrifying kind of chaos.

The ensemble cast is a strong one, headlined by John Malkovich, Tobias Menzies, Yumi Asō, Maria Bakalova, and more.

Apple’s slate of originals is currently light on romantic comedies, but the talent behind Prodigies gives the show a lot of promise. I’m excited to learn more as February draws closer.

title: Pixel 11 series still not on Android 17 QPR1 with October update
snippet: With yesterday’s October 2026 update, the Pixel 11 series is not yet running Android 17 QPR1. more…
fullText:
With yesterday’s October 2026 update, the Pixel 11 series is not yet running Android 17 QPR1.

The Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold launched in August with the base Android 17 release. In September, the Pixel 11 series received two early updates that presumably addressed issues that emerged since launch. 

	

Later in the month, Google rolled out QPR1 to all other devices. Visual changes in the quarterly release include system blur for the volume slider and power menu, while there’s an updated system media player that gets narrower when other apps are available. The Mobile Data Quick Settings Tile gets a time-saving “Don’t ask me again” toggle, while there’s now a Keyboard QS Tile.

Meanwhile, the Pixel 11 series did not get the initial Android 17 QPR2 Beta 6 release and had to wait a few days for Beta 6.1, which introduced HiLight support for message notifications. It did get the 17 QPR3 Beta without issue a few days later. 

	

This week’s October release does contain fixes for the Pixel 11:

Fix for issue causing the virtual keyboard to occasionally not appear when interacting with search input fields*[1]

Fix for issue occasionally causing captured photos or recorded videos to save in the incorrect orientation*[3]

It’s unlikely that we’ll get a second October release, with all eyes on November. With QPR2 just a month away at that point, Google might wait for December to align all the devices.

title: Apple, Prosser, and Ramacciotti trade blame over delays in trade secret lawsuit
snippet: In a joint status report made public earlier today, Apple said it is still waiting on additional documents from Jon Prosser and wants to depose Michael Ramacciotti again, while both defendants pushed back on the company’s handling of the case. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In a joint status report made public earlier today, Apple said it is still waiting on additional documents from Jon Prosser and wants to depose Michael Ramacciotti again, while both defendants pushed back on the company’s handling of the case. Here are the details.

According to a joint status report to Judge James Donato, Apple, leaker Jon Prosser, and Michael Ramacciotti are increasingly at odds over who is responsible for delays in the trade secret lawsuit Apple filed against both defendants in July 2025.

A bit of context

As a refresher, soon after announcing iOS 26, Apple filed a trade secret misappropriation lawsuit against Prosser and Ramacciotti over Prosser’s videos, where he leaked aspects of the system, including what turned out to be the Liquid Glass visual revamp.

Apple said Ramacciotti improperly accessed the development iPhone of an employee, who was later fired over the incident, and held a FaceTime call with Prosser to show him unreleased iOS features running on the device.

Since then, the case has had its own share of drama, with the clerk’s entry of default after Prosser failed to respond to Apple’s complaint by the deadline (although Prosser has disputed the characterization that he had ignored the case).

Then, eight months later, the court agreed to set that default aside and give him another chance to formally contest the allegations.

Court documents show that Ramacciotti, on the other hand, responded to Apple’s complaint and has largely cooperated with the company’s discovery requests.

Since Prosser retained representation and formally entered the case, however, things have taken a turn, with all three sides increasingly disagreeing over who is responsible for the alleged trade secret disclosure and for the delays that have followed.

The new joint status report

Back to the new status report, Apple says it wants Ramacciotti to update his interrogatory responses and sit for another deposition to address what it describes as “inconsistencies between his and Mr. Prosser’s testimony.”

Ramacciotti, however, says he will sit for another deposition once Apple provides “a roadmap to resolution of its claims against him, including what more, if anything, Apple needs from him.”

When it comes to Prosser, Apple says it “continues to await his production of certain additional documents that it requested over three months ago. These include revenue reports and data analytics for his YouTube channels and relevant communications with third parties that he identified during his deposition.”

Prosser, in turn, argues that “[i]t appears that the Trade Secrets at issue are no longer trade secrets and are in the public domain.” In other words, his argument appears to be that since Apple released the iOS update with Liquid Glass, the information at the center of the lawsuit is now publicly available and therefore no longer qualifies as secret.

As part of the joint status update, Ramacciotti asks the court to hold a status conference this month, at which Apple would be required to explain what additional information it still needs from him. He also wants Apple to then have 30 days to either dismiss its claims against him or commit to taking the case to trial.

Apple, meanwhile, wants discovery to continue, including a second deposition of Ramacciotti and the outstanding documents from Prosser. Prosser argues that he has already complied with the discovery obligations he agreed to and pushes back on Apple’s continuing requests for additional material.

If Judge Donato does not grant Ramacciotti’s request for a status conference, the parties propose filing another joint status report on December 2.

title: Amazon’s new Alexa Tablets are an iPad-inspired reboot, complete with the Play Store
snippet: Amazon has an all-new lineup of tablets ready to tempt you this holiday season, and for once, you might actually want to buy them. While the company has tried in previous years to make an upmarket play for relevancy in the tablet space, these new Alexa Tablets — RIP “Fire” — have the one thing everyone’s wanted for years: actual Play Store support. more…
fullText:
Amazon has an all-new lineup of tablets ready to tempt you this holiday season, and for once, you might actually want to buy them. While the company has tried in previous years to make an upmarket play for relevancy in the tablet space, these new Alexa Tablets — RIP “Fire” — have the one thing everyone’s wanted for years: actual Play Store support.

Yes, a decade after ditching the “Kindle” branding in its tablet lineup, Amazon is ditching the Fire brand entirely for its new lineup of iPad competitors. That’s not me trying to write off its Android-powered rivals; rather, the sizes and designs all make for devices that, frankly, look like iPad knock-offs. Alexa Tablets come in three sizes: an 8-inch entry-level iPad Mini competitor, an 11-inch base iPad-esque slate, and a 12-inch “Pro” model that looks to be the most unique of the bunch. They’re all designed with aluminum bodies and, despite being much more expensive than the Fire tablets they’re replacing, still manage to undercut most of the market.

The 8.7-inch 60Hz Alexa Tablet 8 features 4GB of RAM, up to 128GB of storage, and comes in graphite, rosette, and teal, while the 90Hz 11-inch Alexa Tablet 11 features 8GB of RAM, up to 128GB of storage, and adds matcha and amethyst to the mix. Both run on a MediaTek 8189 8-core processor, a relatively recent chipset that appeared in a handful of seemingly-unreleased ChromeOS devices over the past year or so, before landing in these budget tablets. While I wouldn’t say there’s much to write home here about the specs — and again, the design is just absolutely a blatant copy of the iPad — it certainly sounds like a big upgrade over their predecessors.

	

And really, that comes down to the software. Despite Amazon’s current Android-less strategy on its Fire TV devices, the company seems to be doubling down on Android with its tablets. While it does have a unique launcher designed to push Alexa+, these things run proper Android, complete with the Play Store front and center on the device. YouTube is one of the highlighted apps on their store listings, and as someone who maintained Play Store sideloading guides at two different tech websites over the past decade, I can certainly say I never saw it coming. I have no idea how the actual software experience will feel day-to-day, but in terms of app support, it’s one problem that’s finally solved.

	

The star of the show, of course, is the 12-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. This is, bar none, the most premium tablet Amazon has ever shipped, with a price that matches. It combines a 2.8K 3:2 120Hz display with quad speakers, 8GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, and a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 processor. That’s a real processor, and while I wouldn’t say it’s worthy of being called a flagship chipset, it’s undoubtedly the most powerful chip Amazon’s ever used. It’s a good sign when you’re using the same processor that a budget gaming-focused brand like Poco used just a year or two ago.

The 12-inch model also comes in an optional “nanomatte” version for an anti-glare experience, which also allows you to upgrade your RAM and storage to 16GB and 256GB, respectively. 16GB of RAM in an Amazon tablet — it’s a new day after all. And like its last attempt to go full-premium, the company does offer optional stylus and keyboard accessories for road warriors on a budget.

The Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $230 for the base 64GB model with lockscreen ads, or $250 without, while the Alexa Tablet 11 starts at $330 for its base model, or $350 for the ad-free version. Both feature a 128GB upgrade for $50 more. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $500 for the base 128GB model; the nanomatte upgrade will run you $50 more. Meanwhile, that high-end 16/256 variant costs a whopping $680, and while that might sound pretty expensive on paper, it comes in well under Samsung’s latest 12-inch tablet for anyone who doesn’t need that level of processing power. Oh, and absolutely no ads on any of the 12 Pro models — the price you see is the price you pay, no upgrades necessary.

title: HomeView and More: Everything Apple Announced at Its ‘Welcome Home’ Event
snippet: Apple is making a sweeping new entry into home tech.
fullText:
Apple wants to have a much bigger presence in your house. On Tuesday, the company behind Macs and iPhones unveiled a sweeping lineup of new products presenting a range of options for home management, security and entertainment.

The centerpiece is the Apple HomeView smart display, which can sit on a tabletop or be mounted on a wall. In its tabletop version, with its domed base, it echoes the iconic iMac G4 from the early 2000s. 

But this is a device for a new era, brimming with Siri AI and personalization features and built for household interactions.

			

More from CNET

“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing, said in a statement. 

The products altogether represent a big new smart home push for Apple, which for years has largely left that field to be dominated by Amazon and Google. One thing that could work in Apple’s favor, said Ben Wood, chief analyst at FDM CCS Insight, is its reputation for making technology easier to use than the alternatives. 

“In typical Apple fashion, setting up the new products is simple: you just hold your iPhone near the device and add it as easily as pairing new Apple headphones or Watch,” Wood told CNET via email. “That’s quite a contrast to other smart home products where you have to download a specific app, scan QR codes and more.”

Tuesday’s “Welcome Home” event took place just over a month after Apple’s September introduction of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and the folding iPhone Duo.

Here’s everything Apple just announced: 

The HomeView is designed as the hub for a range of capabilities, including making FaceTime calls, playing music and managing smart home devices. 

It has a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display and Apple’s A18 chip. It can also be controlled by touch or voice. Apple sees its new Siri AI as central to the experience of using the HomeView.

It can recognize up to six people by their faces and you can set up a personalized home screen for each. Like on the Apple Watch, display customization options allow for a wide range of screen designs. The Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds simultaneously.

Just like an Apple Watch: You can customize the look of your HomeView, depending on your preference, from standard clocks to calendar to family to Snoopy.Apple

The HomeView works with the new Apple Home Collection devices – more on that below – as well as other Matter and Works with Apple Home accessories

The tabletop version is available in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink and space gray

The wall mount version comes in either silver or space gray.

Preorders start Tuesday for people in the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and India, on Thursday for those in Singapore, and on Friday for those in South Africa, with availability in all those countries beginning Nov. 13. The HomeView isn’t available in EU countries because Siri AI is not available in iOS there.

The HomeView is priced at $299 for both the tabletop and wall-mounted versions. There are two dedicated wall mounts, at $60 and $80, that can be preordered starting Tuesday. A third wall mount will be available in early 2027 for $130.

Apple Home Collection

The Home Collection line of products includes smart home cameras for both indoors and outdoors, thermostats, temperature sensors, a video doorbell and a smart lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. In its press release, Apple described the gear as having a “clean, minimal aesthetic.”

The lineup includes four LG camera devices: 

The $250 Video Doorbell, with dual cameras (for views of visitors and packages), plus a spotlight and a chime that plays through the HomeView, HomePod and HomePod Mini.

The $400 Floodlight Cam, which has motion sensing and low-light color night vision.

The simpler $200 Outdoor Cam. 

The $200 Indoor Cam – for privacy: tilts up and down for you to monitor while you’re away, and down to stop monitoring when you’re at home.

Apple emphasized the privacy aspects of the devices. For instance, the Indoor Cam will tilt down when you’re at home. Camera footage, the company said, is processed locally or via Private Cloud Compute. For those with an iCloud Plus subscription, up to 10 days’ worth of video history can be stored in encrypted form.

The collection also includes the $350 LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, which recognizes when known users approach. It can unlock automatically and can work in conjunction with the video doorbell. 

Two thermostats are in the mix, one from LG and the other from Schneider. Each costs $200, and separate temperature sensors cost $40 apiece. 

Availability for the Home Collection products begins in December, with certain accessories available starting in early 2027.

The new Apple TV 4K can be paired with up to four HomePod speakers.Apple

Apple HomePod Mini 2

Apple is expanding its HomePod line with the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 smart speaker, or as Apple puts it, “conversational assistant.” It’s the first major upgrade to the HomePod lineup in years.

It can sync up with other HomePods or with Apple TV. For first time, the company said, users can create four-speaker surround sound with new Apple TV 4K. Buyers can choose from five colors: pink, green, blue, white and midnight.

“When paired with the new Apple TV 4K, it delivers our most immersive home theater setup yet,” Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of worldwide home product marketing, said in a statement.

Preorders for the HomePod Mini 2 begin Tuesday for people in the US and about two dozen countries and regions, with availability starting Oct. 30. Siri AI access will arrive in a future software update.

Apple TV 4K

The new Apple TV 4K has Apple’s A19 chip, which allows for up to 50% faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance, the company said. Besides streaming shows and movies, it can also serve as a home hub – for instance, doorbell notifications will appear on the screen.

It has three built-in far-field microphones so that you can talk to Siri AI. 

Preorders start Tuesday, with availability Nov. 13 for customers in the US and 29 other countries and regions. Pricing starts at $299 or $49.83 per month for six months.

CNET Principal Writer Katie Collins contributed to this article.

fullText:
The recording device was apparently discovered plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive meeting room.

The recording device was apparently discovered plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive meeting room.

by  Emma Roth

Oct 13, 2026, 8:45 PM UTC

Image: The Verge

Emma Roth

 

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

An OpenAI engineer was arrested after the company said it discovered a “sophisticated recording device” hidden in one of its offices. The employee was identified as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national. Alfozan is charged with using or endeavoring to use a device to intercept oral communications, according to a press release from the Department of Justice.

OpenAI’s post about the incident says it used its AI models to “understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.”

As noted by the DOJ, OpenAI found the device plugged into a TV’s USB port in an executive conference room, where discussions about “highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information” often take place.

Alfozan didn’t have access to this room, but CCTV footage allegedly showed him “near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the device’s discovery,” according to the DOJ. Footage also captured Alfozan appearing to look behind the TV where the device was installed, federal prosecutors claim.

The device was covered in toilet paper and installed on or around September 28th. Its contents were encrypted. Additionally, the DOJ claims OpenAI security discovered a bag Alfozan left in another room inside the company’s office, where they found his wallet, ID, and another recording device.

OpenAI says it fired the employee and referred the incident to the FBI. Alfozan was arrested Friday and has remained in custody since, appearing in federal court for the first time on Tuesday.

We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices. We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.

At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated.

We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.

Update, October 13th: Added information from the DOJ.

title: Apple ‘Welcome home’ event: Three new products are coming tomorrow
snippet: Apple officially confirmed that it will hold a product launch event tomorrow, October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event. more…
fullText:
Apple officially confirmed that it will hold a product launch event tomorrow, October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event.

Apple ‘Welcome home’ details

There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined. There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.”

This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home.

What to expect

‘HomeView’ smart display

Tomorrow’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which Bloomberg says will be called HomeView. Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

According to Bloomberg, the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4.

One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen.

In terms of software, the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode.

Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November. 

New Apple TV 4K

Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip.

That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.

The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it. 

Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV.

HomePod mini 2

The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5.

Beyond the faster chip, the new HomePod mini 2 will reportedly come in new colors:

Pink

White

Green

Blue

Black

Bonus: New ‘second-party’ smart home gear

Finally, Apple is working with LG on new “second-party” accessories for HomeKit. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras.

Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though.

Leaked images reveal Apple’s new Home smart lock, thermostat, more for LG

Wrap up

While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow.

fullText:
Apple TV today announced “Heart,” an original eight-episode true-crime podcast involving two men linked by a donated heart and the same terrible demise. Here are the details.

The lives and deaths of two men linked by a single heart

Although far fewer in number than its movies and series, Apple TV has steadily expanded its lineup of original podcasts since 2021, releasing several titles spanning true crime, investigative journalism, comedy, and companion podcasts for its shows.

That includes “Adrift,” “Unicorn Girl,” “Pluribus: The Official Podcast,” and “Magnificent Jerk.”

Today, the platform announced “Heart,” an eight-episode true-crime original podcast hosted by Karen Kilgariff, set to premiere on October 19.

Here’s Apple TV on what to expect from “Heart”:

When Sonny Graham receives a lifesaving heart transplant, he falls in love with his donor’s widow. What local newspapers hail as a miraculous love story takes a tragic turn when Sonny dies — the same way as his heart donor, Terry Cottle. In both cases, the official conclusion is suicide. As friends and family recall changes in Sonny’s behavior after the transplant, some question whether the heart he received could have carried traces of the donor’s trauma.

Apple TV says “Heart” is the result of years of investigative reporting, with the team behind the podcast piecing together court documents, public records, and firsthand accounts to investigate the circumstances surrounding both men’s deaths and their impact on their families.

Apple TV subscribers will get access to all eight episodes of “Heart” on October 19, while nonsubscribers will get the first three episodes on that date, followed by weekly releases every Monday through November 23.

title: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
snippet: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."
fullText:
OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms.

The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device.

The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices.

“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X.

OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team.

Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office.

Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee.

It’s not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to “capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology.” 

Neither Alfozan nor his attorney could be immediately reached for comment. He faces five years in prison if convicted.

When reached, a spokesperson for the FBI reiterated a statement made by Patel.

“Protecting American SI innovation is essential to safeguarding our nation’s economic strength and national security, and the FBI views that mission as one of our highest counterintelligence priorities,” Patel said.

fullText:
Apple has confirmed a special ‘Welcome home’ product launch event is happening next Tuesday, October 13. But it hasn’t yet said whether there will be a keynote video. Here’s what we know.

Apple hasn’t confirmed ‘Welcome home’ keynote, but Mark Gurman says an ‘online video presentation’ is coming

Apple has been shaking up its typical product launch approaches this year. The MacBook Neo was the first example when it debuted in March with an in-person press “experience” following multiple days of press releases launching other products.

Now Apple’s ‘Welcome home’ launch on October 13 looks set to similarly tread new ground.

Unlike a traditional event, Apple hasn’t yet added ‘Welcome home’ to its Apple Events webpage. And there’s no evidence of a livestream on YouTube or the Apple TV app.

These things could all change in the coming days ahead of the launch. However, currently they indicate there won’t be a keynote video on October 13.

However, Mark Gurman at Bloomberg says a video presentation is coming. In his report about another Apple launch coming October 27, Gurman writes:

Like its smart home event on Oct. 13, the next launch will include an online video presentation and in-person component for the press

So according to Gurman, who accurately reported the October 13 date and its focus on Home products, Apple will have “an online video presentation” next week.

Press are attending a NYC “Apple Experience” that starts at 9:00 a.m. ET. So if there is an announcement video, we’ll likely see it debut online then—much earlier than the typical keynote time.
